title: 3. Distribution, Supply Chain & Unit Economics

epigraph.quote: In hazardous inorganic chemicals, the moat is often written in transport regulations, kiln corrosion curves, and working capital days rather than patent filings.
epigraph.author: Specialty Chemicals Supply Chain Review

web_blocks.html: Tanfac operates a direct B2B industrial distribution model [4]. It maintains zero retail or consumer-facing sales operations [4]. The company supplies over 400 industrial customers across India and ten export destinations [4]. Anhydrous Hydrofluoric Acid is an acutely toxic, corrosive substance classified as UN 1052 [4]. Therefore, it cannot be shipped through standard commercial transport or third-party freight [4]. Tanfac relies on specialized stainless-steel ISO tank containers for bulk deliveries [4]. It uses fluoropolymer-lined drums for ultra-pure Solar DHF and lined road tankers for Oleum [4]. Dedicated hazardous-cargo carriers handle overland movement [4]. This transport complexity creates natural geographic barriers against potential competitors [3][4]. Concurrently, proximity to Cuddalore Port streamlines bulk discharge of imported fluorspar and sulphur [3].

Co-promoter Anupam Rasayan India Limited represents an important strategic partner [1][3]. ARIL acquired a 24.96% stake in March 2022 [1][3]. That transaction secured captive HF and Potassium Fluoride for its agrochemical pipeline [1][3]. Despite this linkage, related-party sales to Anupam Rasayan remain modest [21]. Transferred volumes typically account for 1.88% to 3.57% of annual revenue [21]. All transactions undergo Audit Committee review under SEBI LODR arm's-length pricing rules [21]. Over 95% of total sales flow to independent domestic and export accounts [14][21]. These customers include long-term partners like Kredence Electronics Materials [14]. Arm's-length pricing discipline protects minority shareholder value as Anupam Rasayan expands fluorinated custom synthesis [3][21].

Three globally traded commodities dictate Tanfac's unit input costs [4][20]. These feedstocks are acid-grade fluorspar, elemental sulphur, and potassium carbonate [4][20]. China dominates worldwide acid-spar mining and processing [22]. Chinese environmental curbs or mining crackdowns routinely trigger global price spikes [22]. Elemental sulphur prices also escalated during FY26 [20][23]. Consequently, Tanfac's raw material and packing costs rose 47.4% year-over-year [20][23]. Total material expense increased from ₹307.60 crore in FY25 to ₹453.47 crore in FY26 [20][23]. Customer supply contracts reset prices on monthly or quarterly lags [20]. Rapid input increases therefore compress gross margins during transitional periods [20]. Gross margin dropped from 45.20% in FY25 to 37.46% in FY26 [20]. Operating EBITDA margin compressed further to 11.84% in Q2 FY27 despite record revenue of ₹230.48 crore [8][20].

web_blocks.html: Working capital discipline improved structurally in FY26 as revenue grew 28% [6]. Debtor Days tightened from 65 days in FY25 to 57 days in FY26 [6]. Inventory Days dropped from 112 days to 79 days on faster throughput [6]. Working Capital Days improved from 62 days in FY25 to 34 days in FY26 [6]. However, Days Payable contracted from 48 days to 21 days as Tanfac paid suppliers faster [6]. This supplier acceleration held the Cash Conversion Cycle at 115 days [6]. As a result, FY26 operating cash flow was ₹43 crore against ₹114 crore of EBITDA [6].

web_blocks.title: Unit-Economics Watch: Pass-Through Lags & Payable Compression
paragraphs: In FY25, Tanfac operated in an unusually favorable chemical pricing window [6][20]. Tight AHF supply and moderate raw material costs drove a 45.20% gross margin [6][20]. Operating margin reached 23.52% in that year [6]. Across FY26 and early FY27, gross margins normalized to 37.46% [20]. Higher power and freight costs further reduced profitability [8][20]. Operating margin compressed to 11.84% in Q2 FY27 [8][20].

Operating results depend on Solar-Grade DHF delivering premium pricing [14]. Higher-purity sales must offset underlying fluorspar and sulphur volatility [14][20]. In addition, Days Payable should ideally normalize toward 40–50 days [6]. That supplier normalization would help restore CFO-to-EBITDA conversion above 70% [6].

book_subsections.title: Hazardous Logistics as a Moat, Fluorspar as a Chain
paragraphs: You and I can learn a lot about Tanfac's economics simply by looking at how its product moves. Anhydrous Hydrofluoric Acid boils at 19.5 degrees Celsius and is acutely corrosive. You cannot put it on a regular flatbed truck or store it in a standard warehouse. Tanfac ships directly to more than 400 industrial buyers using pressure-rated stainless-steel ISO tank containers, fluoropolymer-lined drums for ultra-pure solar acid, and specialized hazardous-cargo carriers. That logistics barrier keeps casual traders out of the domestic merchant market, while Cuddalore Port gives Tanfac direct access for unloading bulk imported fluorspar and sulphur.

Another question every minority investor should ask is how much of Tanfac's revenue is captive to co-promoter Anupam Rasayan. In practice, related-party sales have historically stayed modest—roughly 1.9 to 3.6 percent of total sales—and are governed by Audit Committee arm's-length disclosures. Over 95 percent of Tanfac's revenue still goes to third-party industrial clients, including multi-year agreements like the Kredence Solar DHF contract.

Yet that third-party exposure brings real input-cost sensitivity. China dominates global acid-grade fluorspar production, and elemental sulphur prices swing with global refining and fertilizer cycles. In FY25, benign input costs and tight domestic AHF supply handed Tanfac a 45.2 percent gross margin. In FY26, sulphur and raw material bills jumped 47 percent to ₹453.47 crore, squeezing gross margins down to 37.5 percent. Look at the quarterly progression: sales doubled from ₹112 crore in September 2024 to ₹230 crore in September 2026, yet absolute operating profit sat flat at ₹27 crore as operating margins compressed from 28 percent at the December 2024 peak down to 11.84 percent in September 2026. Pass-through lags and rising power and freight bills remind us that unit spreads still drive quarterly earnings.

book_subsections.title: Follow Every ₹100 Through the FY26 P&L
paragraphs: Let us walk through the audited FY26 waterfall for every ₹100 of revenue Tanfac billed on its ₹711 crore top line. Raw materials and packing consumed ₹63.78 right off the top—₹435.84 crore for raw materials and ₹17.63 crore for packing. Employee expenses took just ₹3.89, or ₹27.63 crore in total, showing how capital-intensive rather than labor-intensive this continuous-process plant is. Power, fuel, freight, and other operating overheads took another ₹16.30, leaving ₹16.03 in operating EBITDA.

From that ₹16.03, depreciation claimed ₹2.39—up sharply from ₹10 crore to ₹17 crore because the new AHF and Solar DHF units were capitalized—interest took ₹0.84, other income added ₹0.28, and corporate taxes took ₹3.23, leaving ₹9.85 in reported net profit, or ₹70 crore for the year. Now look at cash: even though Working Capital Days improved from 62 days to 34 days as inventory turned faster from 112 days down to 79 days and Debtor Days tightened from 65 to 57, Tanfac paid its suppliers much quicker, cutting Days Payable from 48 days to 21 days. As a result, only ₹6.05 per ₹100 of sales converted into operating cash flow—₹43 crore in total—while capital expenditure consumed ₹11.53 per ₹100 of sales, or ₹82 crore, leaving free cash flow negative at ₹39 crore during the buildout.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The ₹100 waterfall exposes the central forensic truth of Tanfac in FY26: accounting net profit (₹70 crore) looked healthy, but faster supplier payments and heavy capex meant the business consumed ₹39 crore of free cash. That is why management tapped equity markets for ₹349.41 crore in 2026 rather than funding a ₹495 crore HFC-32 plant solely on debt.

book_paragraphs: In specialty chemicals, a factory is only half the moat; the other half is how you source raw materials, move hazardous molecules safely, and convert an invoice into cash. Let us trace Tanfac's supply chain from port to customer gate. Tanfac's primary feedstock, acid-grade fluorspar (calcium fluoride), is largely imported from China, South Africa, and Morocco because India lacks commercial-grade fluorspar deposits. That single fact creates an ever-present raw material and logistics sensitivity: freight rates, Chinese export quotas, and currency movements feed directly into Tanfac's cost of goods sold.

On the second major input—sulphur—Tanfac operates its own Sulphuric Acid and Oleum plants at Cuddalore. Not only does captive sulphuric acid feed the rotary kilns to make HF, it also generates exothermic steam that powers parts of the complex, lowering energy costs. Yet when global sulphur prices spike—as happened in FY26 and into Q2 FY27—that cost inflation still hits gross margins whenever customer contracts re-price with a lag.

Now look closely at our deterministic ₹100 revenue-to-free-cash-flow waterfall for FY26. Out of every ₹100 of revenue (₹711.07 crore total), roughly ₹63.77 goes to raw materials consumed, ₹3.89 to employee costs, and ₹16.31 to other operating, power, and freight expenses, leaving ₹16.03 of EBITDA. After depreciation (₹2.25), minimal interest (₹0.42), other income (+₹0.70), and taxes (₹3.52), net profit lands at ₹9.86 per ₹100 of sales. Here is the catch: when you move from accounting profit to cash flow, working capital absorbed cash as days payable compressed from 48 days to 21 days. Cash flow from operations was just ₹6.05 per ₹100 of sales (₹43 crore total), and after ₹11.53 per ₹100 of capital expenditure (₹82 crore), free cash flow was negative ₹5.48 per ₹100. That waterfall tells you everything about why capex-heavy chemical companies require patient cash monitoring.

Step back and look at the logistics ballet required at Cuddalore every single day. Imported acid-grade fluorspar arrives at nearby ports, is trucked into SIPCOT Cuddalore, and is blended with captive sulphuric acid inside heated rotary kilns to liberate hydrogen fluoride gas. That gas is scrubbed, condensed, and distilled into anhydrous liquid HF stored in pressurized bullets, or absorbed into ultra-pure deionized water for Solar-Grade DHF.

From a working-capital perspective, that manufacturing chain ties up cash in three places: imported fluorspar inventory buffers against shipping delays, work-in-process and finished-goods tanks, and trade receivables from industrial buyers. When suppliers demand faster payment—pushing Tanfac's Days Payable down from 48 days to 21 days in FY26—cash gets squeezed out of working capital even while the income statement prints ₹114 crore of EBITDA. That is why our ₹100 waterfall shows ₹6.05 of operating cash flow per ₹100 of sales despite ₹9.86 of net profit.

Think about what happens inside the Cuddalore unit economics whenever global shipping lanes tighten or sulphur prices spike. Because acid-grade fluorspar travels by sea from China, South Africa, or Morocco, port congestion or export duties force Tanfac to carry higher safety stock. Meanwhile, on the finished-product side, transporting pressurized Anhydrous HF requires dedicated ISO tankers and trained hazardous-material drivers, limiting the radius over which bulk acid can be shipped economically before freight eats into contribution margin. That geographic reality makes co-locating downstream plants—like Solar-Grade DHF and the upcoming HFC-32 unit—right inside Cuddalore's fence line a huge structural advantage, because captive HF flows by pipeline rather than highway tanker.
